q: The saddlepoint approximation in statistics gives a highly accurate approximation to density functions via the cumulant generating function K(t) = log E[e^{tX}]. The saddlepoint density is:
opts: p(x) ≈ e^{K(t̂) − t̂x} · (2πK''(t̂))^{-1/2} where t̂ solves K'(t̂) = x
exp: Saddlepoint approximation: p̂(x) = (2πK''(t̂))^{-1/2} exp(K(t̂) − t̂x) where K'(t̂) = x. This is extremely accurate (relative error O(1/n) vs O(1/√n) for CLT) and is derived from the Legendre-Fenchel duality between the CGF K and the rate function I(x) = sup_t{tx − K(t)}.
